conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and maintaining a substantial cash buffer, aiming for steady, low-drawdown performance.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech, while keeping leverage small and maintaining a moderate cash buffer to manage drawdowns.

plan: Add to SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged exposure in semiconductors and space.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell all SOXL and SPAL to eliminate high-beta and leveraged exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and covered-call ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Maintain a 10% cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index for steady distributions, while cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs, so this is not a savings account.
